 GOAL Christian Pulisic buries a bicycle kick and Julian Hall delivers his best goal yet - USMNT winners and losers from Mauricio Pochettino’s farewell win over Haiti
 Weston McKennie set up both goals as the Americans beat Haiti 2-0. A late yellow card will keep Sebastian Berhalter out of the CONCACAF Nations League semifinal in March.
 Ryan Tolmich 4 hours ago Last updated 4 hours ago Share Share CINCINNATI -- Mauricio Pochettino’s U.S. Men’s National Team swansong brought more of the same: more highlights, more goals and one last clinical win before his departure for Manchester.
 Following on the heels of the 6-0 beatdown of Haiti on Saturday, the USMNT cruised past the same opponent on Tuesday in Cincinnati. This time, the scoreline was a mere 2-0, but it was a game that largely went as expected with the USMNT dominating long stretches and, ultimately, leaving with a pretty straightforward win.
 The goals the USMNT scored weren't straightforward, though; they were spectacular. The first came off the foot of Christian Pulisic, who netted his third in two games with a fantastic bicycle kick. Julian Hall joined him on the scoresheet before halftime with a stunner of his own, dazzling with a series of touches and a striker's finish that put the game out of reach before halftime. 
 As a result, the USMNT march into the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, as expected, as they solidified their next opportunity to become the region's top dogs. That chance will come without Pochettino, though, as someone else prepares to take the helm. All week long, Pochettino stated his intentions of leaving the team in the right place and, with the win on Tuesday, he did just that, handing the next coach plenty of momentum and a chance at a trophy on his way out the door.
 GOAL takes a look at the Winners and Losers of the USMNT's win over Haiti...
 WINNER: Christian Pulisic
 IMAGO / Ball Raw Images The USMNT's star continued to showcase his incredible talent with a stunning goal. 
 What a goal.
 Pulisic has no shortage of good ones in a USMNT shirt, but technically, this was one of his best. His bicycle kick to open the scoring was as impressive as they come, and it was a goal few players can score. Pulisic isn't like most players, though, and these two games have been a reminder of that.
 Is he still catching flak for this summer? Yes. Is that going away any time soon? Sure isn't. Still, even the biggest critics need to be impressed with a goal like Tuesday's, one that will certainly end up on his highlight reel.
 Loser: Cavan Sullivan
 IMAGO / Ball Raw Images The teenager made a youthful mistake before he even stepped on the field.
 Early on in camp, Sullivan said how excited he was to play with Pulisic. Not only did he not get that chance, he got booked just for coming on!
 Sullivan replaced Pulisic midway through the second half and, in his excitement, apparently ran onto the field a bit too soon for the referee's liking. As a result, he was given a yellow card before the ball was even kicked. It was a youthful mistake from USMNT's youngest-ever goalscorer. 
 A learning moment, then, and a good time to learn it. It'll surely be one Sullivan looks back on and laughs at some point.
 WINNER: Julian Hall
 IMAGO / Ball Raw Images Halls scored another goal as his red-hot start continues.
 Keep lining 'em up and Hall will keep knocking 'em down.
 Through his first six USMNT appearances, the striker is now at five goals, and Tuesday's was his best one yet. Played in by Weston McKennie, Hall dazzled with his initial touches before looping a shot around goalkeeper Alexandre Pierre. It was a pure striker's finish preceded by several No. 10-worthy touches.
 Even aside from the goal, Hall was active and involved all through the first half. He routinely made dangerous runs and got the hockey assist on the USMNT's opener, although much of the hard work still had to be done on that one. Still, this was a complete performance from Hall, who looks more and more like a complete striker by the day.
 LOSER: Sebastian Berhalter
 IMAGO / Anadolu Agency Berhalter will miss the CONCACAF Nations League semifinal after taking a yellow card.
 With the score at 8-0 on aggregate and only 20 minutes remaining, Berhalter took a yellow card. It was a silly foul given the state of the game. It was even sillier considering what it cost him.
 With that yellow card, Berhalter will now be suspended for the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals in March. That comes due to his yellow card in each game, with the two-caution accumulation earning him that one-match ban for the next game of the competition.
 Realistically, the USMNT midfield is talented enough to survive, and who even knows what the next coach will want from that midfield? Still, regardless of what that coach wants, he won't have Berhalter at his disposal because of a silly foul four months prior in a game that had long been won.
 Winner: Weston McKennie
 IMAGO / Ball Raw Images McKennie ran the game from his place in midfield.
 If you only saw the goalscorers, you weren't really paying attention. It was McKennie who was running the game, dropping passes all over the field to give those goalscorers the chances they need.
 McKennie assisted both of the USMNT goals in the first half, and both assists were fantastic. The first saw him dart to the end line and cross from a tight angle, finding a leaping Pulisic for the goal. Then, as the half continued, McKennie played an even better ball over the top for Hall, allowing the New York Red Bulls star the opportunity to do the rest.
 In that first half, he had more touches than any other player, won the ball back three times and nearly scored a goal of his own on a close-range header. This was McKennie at his best: active, involved and making things happen all over the field in ways only he can.
